decisions.reason: Selecting the satin finish and gold distribution does not change the required geometric peak alignment between the Hero V and É accent.
Applying champagne gold to three elements does not change the shared terminal geometry, terminal intent, or revision policy.
The source explicitly uses the existing geometry and selects only its material treatment; it does not alter the locked Hero V construction.
Gold on the second V right arm changes material application, not the second V's optically designed geometry or relationship to the Hero V.
Keeping non-gold elements black does not revise the E and L letterform construction, originality, or architectural-language constraints.
The stated visual-hierarchy benefit describes the selected material distribution and does not change the second V's established scale or height relationships.
Applying champagne gold to the É accent does not change its required one-to-one vector derivation from the Hero V terminal.

The source message separately changes kerning, and that change is already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY; the material-treatment source Event requires no additional kerning update.
The selected finish and gold distribution do not change the E/L cap-height rule relative to the second V's left arm.
Material selection does not change the established common-baseline alignment of the wordmark.
The material-treatment decision neither changes nor removes the obligation to explain design intentions during review rounds.
